exposure: Gestational age at delivery (late preterm vs. term)
outcome: Duration of the second stage of labor
Third- and fourth-degree perineal laceration rates
Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: 10,438 women with singleton pregnancy, vertex presentation, spontaneous or induced onset of labor, who delivered vaginally beyond 34.0 weeks of gestation.
finding: Women who delivered vaginally during the late preterm period had a significantly shorter second stage of labor compared to those who delivered at term, especially among nulliparous women and multiparous women without epidural use.
gest_age: Late preterm (34.0-36.6 weeks) and term (≥37 weeks)
birth_weight: Birth weight at delivery was a factor influencing the duration of the second stage of labor
